title: High winter river flows decreased young-of-year brown trout catches at 579 English sites in 1991-2025; Atlantic salmon had the same sign, but the interval included zero
abstract: Question: do high winter river flows decrease young-of-year (0+) salmonid numbers in English rivers? Data: Environment Agency electric-fishing surveys (NFPD counts and individual lengths, 1991-2025) and EA daily mean river flow from 776 matched gauges. Method: 0+ fish were separated by region-month length cut-offs calibrated on staff age labels. The outcome was log(1 + 0+ first-run catch per 100 m2). The exposure was the Dec-Mar peak daily flow relative to the gauge median. Models had site and year fixed effects, survey-day flow, summer low flow, spring peak, survey date, area and method controls, and two-way clustered errors. The plan was written before the outcome models. Results: for brown trout (6,154 site-years, 579 sites) the slope was -0.139 (95% CI -0.223 to -0.054): a peak two times the usual peak came before about 13% fewer 0+ trout at the median catch. All four region-period sub-samples were negative. The next-winter placebo (+0.007) and older trout (+0.004) gave no effect. The slope held with region-year effects, river-matched gauges, spawner and winter temperature controls. For Atlantic salmon (3,317 site-years) the slope was -0.114 (CI -0.264 to +0.035), uncertain. An exploratory window model put the largest effect in February-March (salmon -0.181, CI -0.263 to -0.100). Winter peaks rose 0.07 log units per decade (CI included zero), which implies only about 3% fewer 0+ trout over 1991-2025, while observed 0+ year effects increased. Limitations: observational design, nearest-gauge matching without a river network, first-run catch is not abundance, depletion-only fits were weaker, and the sites are a non-random subset. No air pollutant was tested.

display.caption: Slope of 0+ catch, log(1 + catch per 100 m2), on the December-March peak-flow index, with 95% intervals, for brown trout (blue) and Atlantic salmon (orange): main model, four planned region-period sub-samples, next-winter placebo, older-fish outcome and robustness checks.
Exploratory model (not in the plan): peak-flow indices of four two-month windows in one model. The February-March window gave the most negative slope for both species.

Top: mean winter peak-flow index at the sample gauges by year. Bottom: 0+ year effects from a site fixed-effects model without flow terms (centred). The 0+ year effects did not follow the small rise in winter peaks.
